item.title: 'Not once have people really mentioned Matt Kuhnemann': Usman Khawaja on Australia’s Test Selection dilemma
item.description: Former Australia opener Usman Khawaja has urged selectors to consider left-arm spinner Matt Kuhnemann for the decisive final Test against South Africa in Cape Town. With the series now level at 2-1, Australia need to get their team selection right after suffering a heavy defeat in the previous match. Australia left experienced spinner Nathan Lyon out of the Gqeberha Test and picked fast bowler Scott Boland instead. Boland performed well, taking five wickets, but Australia’s decision to play without a frontline spinner backfired as South Africa won by an innings and 31 runs. Khawaja backs Kuhnemann for final Test Khawaja believes Kuhnemann deserves a chance, especially because South Africa have several right-handed batters. The left-arm spinner has played five Tests and already taken a five-wicket haul. Although he has not played a Test since February 2025, he impressed during Australia’s tour of Sri Lanka, finishing the two-match series with 16 wickets. “We’ve talked about Boland and Lyon (in the second Test), and not once have people really mentioned Kuhnemann. He is a terrific bowler, a Test bowler. He has a Test five-fa, and done really well for Australia when he’s played,” Khawaja told foxsports.com.au. He explained that Kuhnemann could trouble right-handed batters by making the ball spin away from them, much like South African spinner Simon Harmer troubled Australia’s left-handers. “I know Nathan Lyon’s the ‘GOAT’, and there’s nothing against the GOAT! This is purely based on the fact the South Africans have so many right-handers in their team. I think Kuhnemann deserves to be talked about,” Khawaja added. Khawaja weighs in on Australia’s batting options Australia also face questions about their batting order ahead of the series decider. Selectors must decide whether Nic Maddinson should continue opening, where Marnus Labuschagne should bat and how to fit Cam Green back into the team as he nears a return from injury. Khawaja believes Maddinson could be more effective in the middle order, where he can face spin bowling rather than handle the difficult task of opening the innings. “No discredit to Nic Maddinson. I think Maddinson is terrific. I actually would have put him in the middle order at the start of the series, purely based on the fact the opening is so hard of a gap to fill,” Khawaja concluded.

item.title: Colts GM search gets big Peyton Manning update from Adam Schefter
item.description: Colts GM search gets big Peyton Manning update from Adam Schefter originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts fired long-time general manager Chris Ballard after the team's Week 6 loss to the Tennessee Titans . That decision has opened up a very interesting GM job in the NFL. This Colts team is in a bit of trouble, and managing the team out of this hole will prove tricky. But who will be the one to take over for Ballard? Well, one name emerged recently that caused plenty of buzz: former Colts quarterback Peyton Manning. However, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Colts are not expected to get Manning as their general manager, as the Hall of Famer and now ESPN talent is not expected to become the new Colts GM. Peyton Manning not expected to take Colts GM job "Peyton Manning has many jobs -- Omaha Productions, the ManningCast, commercial pitchman -- but he is not expected to add Indianapolis Colts general manager to his list of titles and responsibilities, league sources told ESPN," Schefter reports. While there was some obvious appeal to bringing in Manning as the new general manager, this report from Schefter should end that speculation and hope for Colts fans. Schefter also reported that Indianapolis hadn't even reached out to Manning about the job, and that Manning wouldn't be interested if given the opportunity. While the Colts might ask for his advice on a new GM hire, or help in some capacity with how to run the team, this doesn't look like it's going to become a John Elway situation. MORE : Why Colts are likely sellers after firing Chris Ballard before NFL trade deadline The Colts, in their search for a general manager to get them out of the mess that Ballard helped create, will have someone not named Peyton Manning in the GM chair leading the way. This shouldn't be a huge surprise, as the rumors linking Manning to the Colts GM job were only just rumors. Carlie Irsay-Gordon has some work to do, as the Colts search for a new GM comes with the team potentially set to be major sellers at this year's trade deadline. A new GM likely won't be hired until after the deadline, and potentially not until the season is over. But whoever is set to take over, they'll have their work cut out for them with this roster in need of a major overhaul. item.title: Gavi reveals his true feelings about Real Madrid and Mourinho ahead of El Clasico: ‘Like having him as an opponent’
item.description: Gavi reveals his true feelings about Real Madrid and Mourinho ahead of El Clasico: ‘Like having him as an opponent’ Real Madrid have received a clear message from Barcelona ahead of Sunday’s El Clasico , with Gavi insisting that the absence of Vinicius Jr. will not reduce his determination to beat Los Blancos . The Barcelona midfielder also expressed his admiration for Jose Mourinho, while teammate Rodri warned that Madrid remain dangerous regardless of their inconsistent La Liga form. The comments, made in interviews with ESPN (h/t AS ) ahead of the meeting at Camp Nou, come at a crucial point in the title race. Barcelona could move nine points clear of their rivals with victory, placing additional pressure on Mourinho’s Real Madrid project. Gavi dismisses Real Madrid absences ahead of Clasico Gavi has developed a reputation for his intensity in matches against Real Madrid, and Vinicius’ absence means one of the rivalry’s most familiar individual duels will not take place this time. Gavi is not bothered by Vinicius’ absence. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Asked about Madrid missing the Brazilian, the Barcelona midfielder made clear that the opposition’s personnel would not change his approach. “A weakened side without Vinicius? I don’t care. It’s Real Madrid and, at the end of the day, I’ll give it my all whoever’s playing.” Gavi also explained how much a victory would mean to Barcelona supporters, adding, “There’ll be players I get on better or worse with, but on the pitch I don’t like any of them. I just hope to give the fans a win; they deserve it.” Gavi’s respect for Mourinho Despite his combative attitude towards Real Madrid’s players, Gavi spoke positively about Mourinho’s personality. The Barcelona midfielder said he enjoys facing a coach who is outspoken and brings a strong character to the touchline. Gavi respects Jose Mourinho. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) “I like Mourinho when he speaks. I like that sort of manager – someone with character and a fiery temperament. “I like having him as an opponent. I have a lot of respect for him. The truth is, he doesn’t get on my nerves.” Gavi also described his frustration when injuries prevent him from playing, revealing the depth of his feelings about the rivalry. “When I’m injured, I suffer a lot watching the matches. I can’t bear to watch them. “I want Barça to win and Real Madrid to lose. In my family, we’ve never been fond of Real Madrid,” he concluded.

item.title: Will Byron Young get a sack (or two) against Raiders?
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 20: Gardner Minshew #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders runs with the ball from Byron Young #0 of the Los Angeles Rams during the fourth quarter at SoFi Stadium on October 20, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Joe Scarnici/Getty Images) | Getty Images Will Byron Young have a massive game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday? Young has been a good player for the Los Angeles Rams, he’s been great at times, but this year the defense isn’t generating enough sacks. That includes Young. The team is getting pressure, but the defense and Young need to finish with sacks. Pressures aren’t enough against the best quarterbacks in the league. It’s been a theme for 2026 that this Rams team is good some important areas. They are generating yards, they are holding teams out of the endzone, there are positive in this 2-4 season. But the Rams aren’t scoring enough points to win, and the defense isn’t making the key stops at the end of games. The special teams are a mess. So, can the Rams get right on Sunday? Young having a big game would help. 3 Bold Predictions in the Los Angeles Rams’ Showdown With Kirk Cousins and the Raiders (athlonsports) “ Los Angeles Rams fans will make the drive up I-15 this weekend for a team that badly needs a road win. The Rams are 2-4 after an 18-16 loss to Arizona, they’ve lost Davante Adams for six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, and Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders are waiting at Allegiant Stadium. Sean McVay has said the Rams’ depth can handle it for now. Byron Young sacks Kirk Cousins twice Byron Young has 29 pressures, sixth among 115 edge defenders, and his 22 hurries lead the position, according to PFF . He has only four sacks, though, and the Rams have just eight as a team despite one of the league’s best pressure rates. They turn pressure into sacks just under 10% of the time, second-worst in the NFL , and we called the pressure-to-sack gap the first fix before Cousins this week.“ Top Rams News: Previews and predictions for Rams at Raiders on Sunday in Las Vegas for Week 7 (therams.com) “Here’s a collection of analysts’ predictions and previews for Rams-Raiders: Nine of the 11 ESPN experts chose the Rams to come out on top on Sunday against the Raiders. Six of the eight Sports Illustrated staffers picked the Rams to win against the Raiders. item.title: 'If it was up to me, it wouldn't have ended like this': James Anderson reacts to bitter end to his 25-year Lancashire career.
item.description: 'If it was up to me, it wouldn't have ended like this': James Anderson reacts to bitter end to his 25-year Lancashire career. originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: England legend James Anderson's 25-year Lancashire career ends as the club declines to extend his contract. Anderson said it would not have ended this way had the decision been his. He took 443 first-class wickets for Lancashire and captained them in 2026. James Anderson says his Lancashire exit was not his decision James Anderson has made clear that the end of his Lancashire career came from the club rather than from him. Posting on Instagram after the announcement, the 44-year-old described a quarter of a century at Emirates Old Trafford and then let one line carry the rest. "I've supported Lancashire since I was kid, and so to get to play for them for 25 years was a dream come true," Anderson wrote , before turning to the ground where the whole career was spent. "If it was up to me it wouldn’t have ended like this" - James Anderson on his 25-year Lancashire career coming to an end 🌹 pic.twitter.com/91BY08poeC — Cricinfo (@cricinfo) October 25, 2026 He mentioned the memories of walking out there, including captaining the side for the first time last summer, and only then addressed how it ended. "If it was up to me it wouldn't have ended like this, but I wish the players and fans all the best for the future," he said. Lancashire confirmed on Sunday that his playing career with the club would end when his current contract expires. Anderson made his debut in 2001 as a homegrown bowler from Burnley and took 443 first-class wickets in 112 appearances, along with 83 in List A cricket and 50 in T20 cricket. MORE: 'I know the feeling' - Sammy brings up IND's chase of 406 after SL chases 430 vs ENG Paul Farbrace says the rebuild could not wait The decision was delivered in person. Incoming director of cricket Paul Farbrace met Anderson and chief executive Richard Kenyon at Old Trafford on Monday, October 19, and told him the contract would not be extended for 2027. item.title: John Mateer explains what made him wake up ‘in the middle of the night’ before Sooners win
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images John Mateer and the Sooners have not had the kind of season Oklahoma faithful would have hoped for, but he did deliver an excellent performance against Mississippi State. Mateer and the Sooners knew that the SEC was supposed to be competitive and that they would have to struggle in one of the toughest conferences in the country. However, given the rich heritage and history that the Sooners have as a college football powerhouse, a win was huge for the Sooners coming into the weekend. John Mateer shares inspirational post-game comments after Sooners win Speaking to reporters after the game, Oklahoma Sooners QB John Mateer explained how he overcame difficult experiences before and during games. He noted that he embraced his previous issues coming into the game, along with any possible mistakes he made during the game, with a mentality of forgiveness and focusing on the next opportunity instead. Mateer said: “I woke up in the middle of the night and something told me to forgive yourself. It was really powerful stuff. I hope everybody hears that. I knew when it happened. Forgive yourself, and next play matters. “All day, all I thought was the least important thing. The least important thing just happened. So the next play, focus on being calm and believing in who I am. I think I said earlier this week that I know who I am as a player and as a man. “Through struggle, that’s what you find. I’m not perfect and I won’t be perfect moving forward. But I felt good out there and I believed.” This mindset seems to have paid off for Mateer, who delivered a strong performance in the Sooners’ 23-15 win over Mississippi State. He threw for 283 yards with two touchdowns, with a QB rating of 89.0. The Sooners will be hoping to win their next game to make sure they can win consecutive games for the first time this season. If a suspension comes, the six games he missed would count toward it, according to packers.com . Wisconsin Sports Heroics has covered the legal side of the case since the summer. On the legal side, small details were his point. “Legally, man, I mean, a lot of things can be perceived a certain type of way. And that’s just me not even knowing that, like, small detailed things can be perceived a certain type of way,” Jacobs said. “Legally, it could be a thing that you might not never would even thought was a thing. item.title: Why the Milwaukee Bucks have trusted Kasparas Jakucionis to close out their first 2 games this season
item.description: Kasparas Jakucionis was part of the haul the Milwaukee Bucks received in the blockbuster Giannis Antetokounmpo trade this summer, and the 20-year-old combo guard is making the most of his opportunity with his new NBA team. Many expected Jakucionis to be a fringe player, but the Illinois product hasn’t played like one thus far. In his first two games of the 2026-27 campaign, Jakucionis has been part of the Milwaukee Bucks’ closing lineup against the Washington Wizards and Chicago Bulls, despite not starting, and he could do the same against the Philadelphia 76ers later. Kasparas Jakucionis’ performances with the Milwaukee Bucks so far Oct 23, 2026; Milwaukee, WI, USA; Chicago Bulls guard Tre Jones (30) is guarded at midcourt by Milwaukee Bucks guard Kasparas Jakucionis (25) during the third quarter at Fiserv Forum. Mandatory Credit: Brad Repplinger-Imagn Images Before the regular season started, Kasparas Jakucionis did well in preseason, averaging 10.3 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 5.3 assists, albeit on 36.8 percent shooting from the field in three appearances. What’s noticeable about the former No. 20 pick is that he has worked on attacking downhill, applying rim pressure, and creating plays for his teammates this summer. Against Washington, Jakucionis contributed 15 points, three rebounds, three assists, and a block on 4-for-7 shooting in 26 minutes. He followed it up by recording seven points, five assists, and two steals on 2-for-4 shooting in 23 minutes against Chicago last night. Milwaukee Bucks’ Tyler Herro not surprised at Kasparas Jakucionis’ growth Tyler Herro has been teammates with Kasparas Jakucionis in the past few months, and the Milwaukee Bucks star strongly believes Jakucionis earned his minutes under head coach Taylor Jenkins. Herro particularly praised Jakucionis for his basketball IQ, energy, and ability to mesh well with the other guards. “He’s a hard worker at the end of the day. He wants to learn. He wants to get better. The sky’s the limit for him. He’s a very smart player. He’s someone that I trust with the ball at the end of the game, so I can see why Coach (Jenkins) does as well,” Herro said of Jakucionis. But through six weeks, they led the AFC North with a 4-2 record and have been a lot better than anticipated. While Deshaun Watson not playing horribly is a big reason for the team's record, the really impressive unit is the defense. Despite losing Garrett, coming off a 23-sack season, this defense has been very impressive. And one of the key cogs just got paid. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , very late Saturday night, the Browns and defensive tackle Maliek Collins reportedly agreed to a $30 million extension, locking up a key lineman for the next few seasons in Cleveland quietly late at night. Browns to sign Maliek Collins to $30M contract extension "Browns and Maliek Collins reached agreement on a 2-year extension worth $30 million, including $23 million in total guarantees, per agent Drew Rosenhaus," Schefter reports. Cleveland, just because they're still looking for a quarterback and might only be a good QB away from being Super Bowl contenders, doesn't mean they can't sign key veterans to extensions. Collins might've been a trade deadline candidate this season had things gone wrong for the Browns. But at 4-2, the Browns are instead set to sign him to an extension. MORE : ESPN analyst believes Browns are a quarterback away from being Super Bowl contenders This season, Collins has been a game-changer from the defensive tackle spot. He has 3.5 sacks with 16 tackles and five tackles for loss with eight quarterback hits in six games played. The 31-year-old veteran, formerly playing for the Dallas Cowboys , Houston Texans , Las Vegas Raiders , and San Francisco 49ers before joining the Browns in 2025, has been a major pass-rushing force in his career. He had a career year in 2025 with the Browns, posting 6.5 sacks, the most in a season. This year, with 3.5 through six games, he's on track to break his previous record for sacks in a season. This Browns season has gone very well so far, and the continued dominance from Collins along the defensive line is a huge reason why. Cleveland agreeing to this $30M extension makes a ton of sense and is a smart move for a team seemingly on the cusp of contention. item.title: McMillan backs Coombes after groin grab allegation
item.description: Gavin Coombes alleged he had been grabbed in the groin late in the first half of Munster's derby defeat by Leinster [Getty Images] Munster head coach Clayton McMillan has backed Gavin Coombes after the number eight alleged he had been grabbed in the groin during Saturday's 24-18 defeat by Leinster. Coombes alleged the incident happened with an unnamed Leinster player at a ruck towards the end of the first half of the United Rugby Championship derby at the Aviva Stadium. Coombes raised the allegation with match referee Andrew Brace, but the television match official (TMO), Colin Stanley, could not find any video evidence of the incident. Speaking after the game, McMillan backed Coombes and, referencing the citing commissioner who can punish retrospective incidents after a review, said it was something that had to be left "for the powers that be". "All I know is that I back our players 100% that if they make an allegation like that, they wouldn't do it lightly," McMillan said. "He's not that sort of person, Gavin, so we'll see where that goes." Leinster head coach Leo Cullen said he did not see the incident but said it was a "serious matter" for the citing commissioner. Cullen also said it "looked like he [Coombes] changed his mind halfway through the accusation". "That's the way it sounded, once the scrum was packing down," said Cullen. "But I don't know. Obviously, once that accusation is made, it becomes a serious matter for the citing commissioner. "My comment is not going to help in any way here, but from what I've seen, I can't see anything."

item.title: Big week for Dortmund: Bremen in Cup and then to Bayern in league
item.description: Borussia Dortmund players celebrate after the Bundesliga soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and Eintracht Frankfurt at Signal Iduna Park. (is associated with: «Big week for Dortmund: Bremen in Cup and then to Bayern in league») Bernd Thissen/dpa Borussia Dortmund approach a crucial week in their season in a confident mood from the knowledge that they have defensive stability and plenty of depth in their squad. Dortmund host Werder Bremen in the German Cup on Tuesday and then visit big rivals Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga on Saturday in what could be a table topper. Saturday's 1-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt kept them unbeaten in the league and was their fifth clean sheet from seven matches. Maximilian Beier scored the late winner after being set up by fellow substitute Jobe Bellingham. "We're not perfect yet, but the team is making progress," defender Nico Schlotterbeck said. "Next week, we're off to take on Bayern. We want to play a strong game there. Before that, we're up against Bremen. They're in good form. I expect a high-intensity affair. The shortest path to silverware is the domestic cup." Tough Cup test before Bayern match Dortmund have the best Bundesliga defence which has let in only four goals, but two of them came two weeks ago against Bremen when they squandered a two-goal lead in the final minutes for a 2-2 draw. "Of course we want to advance," managing director Lars Ricken said ahead of the second-round match where Dortmund will be up against their in-form further player Niclas Füllkrug again, the league top scorer with eight goals. Since last winning the German Cup in 2021 they have not gone further than the quarter-finals. Coach Niko Kovac must balance the workload of his team which has been playing every three days and travelled a lot: including to the Arctic Circle where they lost 1-0 at Bodø/Glimt and then to Azerbaijan for a 2-1 victory against Sabah within seven days, plus a 0-0 Bundesliga draw at Union Berlin in-between. Squad depth helps "You have so many games, and you need a strong roster. In the end, we provided proof of that by having two players come on and make the difference," midfielder Felix Nmecha said. Dortmund have it a little easier as far as travel is concerned with three home games plus the domestic trip to Munich, and Kovac is happy to have plenty of options in the squad. “We’re going through this with our fitness coaches and doctors, of course. We do need to make sure we manage the workload sensibly," Kovac said. “We’ve got a good team; every single player is capable of playing. That’s why you need a good, large squad – and that’s what we’ve got. I’m not worried, no matter who I pick. I know the lads are pushing themselves to the limit.”

item.title: 😨 Derby win before kick-off? Hannover 96 fans get one over on Braunschweig
item.description: 😨 Derby win before kick-off? Hannover 96 fans get one over on Braunschweig The pressure is well and truly on! The Lower Saxony derby between Eintracht Braunschweig and Hannover 96 is hugely important on the pitch, with both teams deep in the relegation mire in the 2. Bundesliga. Neither set of supporters needs reminding of how much this fixture means emotionally, either. That became abundantly clear once again in the build-up to this derby. A few days ago, 96 fans paid a visit to the hall where Braunschweig supporters were working on their tifo display for derby day. The Hannover fans apparently made off with so much material that the display could no longer go ahead as planned. The BTSV ultras left a notice explaining this on the stadium seats before the match. The note reads in part: "A large part of the tifo is no longer in our hands, which would have made putting it on simply impossible. Sometimes you're the dog, sometimes you're the tree – in this case, we're very clearly the ones getting pissed on." At the same time, the Blue and Yellows announced that they would "definitely learn our lessons from this whole affair". We'll be watching with interest to see whether they deliver a response in the stands today – or their players do so on the pitch! This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Good news for Gasperini: Dybala back in training
item.description: Good news for Gasperini: Dybala back in training Paulo Dybala’s first injury of the season came at halftime of the Champions League match between Roma and Real Madrid. The Argentine, who had been suffering from calf pain, was substituted as a precaution and is now working to return to the field as soon as possible. La Joya completed part of the training session with the group today, receiving positive responses from his on-field testing. Gian Piero Gasperini will assess whether he can be counted on for Tuesday’s match against Cagliari or whether he will be available only for the away match in Udine on Saturday, October 31st, at 6:00 PM. If the positive sensations are confirmed, the Giallorossi number 21 could return to the squad for the match against Pisacane’s Rossoblu. Roma met today at Trigoria, where a short recovery session was scheduled for all those who took part in yesterday’s match at the Maradona stadium against Napoli. The rest of the squad was scheduled for a regular training session. After missing the matches against Genoa, Slovan Bratislava, and Napoli, Dybala is working to return to the Giallorossi’s squad as soon as possible. Despite his numerous assists, the Argentine has yet to find the net this season, neither in Serie A nor in the Champions League.

item.title: Toto Wolff Recalls the Savage Insult That Got Him the Mercedes Job: “I’m Just a Messenger”
item.description: Before Mercedes became the unstoppable juggernaut that casually crushed the F1 grid for eight straight years, they were basically just a massively overfunded midfield team setting corporate cash on fire. Back in 2012, the Daimler board was completely baffled as to why their billion-dollar operation was severely underperforming, while a scrappy privateer team like Williams was somehow standing on the top step of the podium. Enter Toto Wolff , who recently dropped a wildly entertaining story on the Cheeky Pint podcast about the savage reality check he delivered to the Mercedes boardroom—a ruthless flex that accidentally landed him the greatest job in motorsport. In 2012, Wolff was an executive and shareholder at Williams during the peak of the Pastor Maldonado era. When Maldonado famously strung together the weekend of his life to win the Spanish Grand Prix, the corporate suits over at Mercedes took notice. “One of the board members approached me and invited me to Stuttgart, and he said, ‘How can it be that your private little team can win a race and we Mercedes, we can’t do any better than that?'” Wolff recalled. The $100 Million Reality Check When Wolff asked the board about their expectations, they immediately demanded World Championships. Wolff bluntly told them their math was completely broken, noting that Williams was operating on the exact same budget but merely aiming for top-six finishes. The board instantly pushed back, arguing that Mercedes actually spent $100 million more than Williams. Wolff’s response was an absolute masterclass in boardroom savagery. Oct 19, 2025; Austin, TX, USA; Mercedes AMG Petronas CEO and team principal Toto Wolff arrives at the track before the start of the 2025 US Grand Prix at Circuit of The Americas Austin. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images “I said, ‘Yeah, those 100 million you spend on Michael Schumacher and Nico Rosberg, I have a paid driver from Venezuela who won the race, by the way, Pastor. That’s the main difference,'” Wolff laughed. It was a brutal truth bomb. Mercedes was burning an insane premium on a seven-time World Champion’s comeback and a highly-rated Rosberg, while Wolff was actively cashing checks from Maldonado’s Venezuelan oil backers—and still matching their results on track. Wolff’s Ultimate Flex Unsurprisingly, a room full of German automotive executives did not appreciate being roasted by the guy from Williams. “So they didn’t like that situation at all. I said I’m just a messenger, you know… and I’m going to go back to Williams,” Wolff said. But instead of throwing him out of the building forever, the Daimler board realized his ruthless, entrepreneurial mindset was exactly what their bloated racing division desperately needed to turn things around. item.title: 49ers legend Terrell Owens’ ‘bad take’ after comparing himself to Mike Evans called out by CB
item.description: Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images San Francisco 49ers legend Terrell Owens seems to have caused a bit of a stir with his take on Mike Evans ‘catching some average plays.’ The legendary wide receiver started his own podcast, Get TO The Point, last month, and the conversation on a recent episode was about Mike Evans, who joined the 49ers after 12 seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He has been impressive and formed a great partnership with quarterback Brock Purdy. However, Terrell Owens seemed to think that there was nothing too excellent about Evans’ performances. “We were watching the game. Mike Evans was playing, and I was like, ‘Look at his routes. I can do that.’ It’s not like he’s blazing speed. He just knows how to run routes, knows where to go, and then the quarterback can save you,” Owens said. “He was just catching some average plays.” Although Owens is a legend in San Francisco, his take did not go down well, especially in the 49ers locker room. Deommodore Lenoir calls out Terrell Owens’ take about Mike Evans Evans is one of the key reasons the team has an unbeaten record. His performance in the clutch against the Seattle Seahawks helped the 49ers get a big win to keep their streak alive. His teammates were not going to let Owens talk him down, which is why Lenoir took to Instagram to share his thoughts on the 52-year-old’s comments. “Mannnn noo you cant,” wrote Lenoir on his Instagram story. “Mike 1 of 1 Stop it. Every WR know where they going. Bad Take.” The six-time Pro Bowler has recorded 420 yards on 20 receptions, despite playing through an injury in the last few games. In his absence, the team struggled in the second half against the Washington Commanders. Evans was injured on the 49ers’ last offensive drive of the first half. They managed to score a touchdown on the same play, but after that looked close to capitulating in the third and fourth quarters. The offence was unable to produce anything significant but they somehow managed to grab a 23-17 win. Evans is set to miss the game against the Atlanta Falcons due to the Achilles tendinitis injury he suffered against the Commanders. Undoubtedly, Owens is one of the best WRs in the NFL. But Mike Evans’ game is different from his. Owens was known for his physical power and speed, whereas Evans is known for his red-zone dominance. However, Lenoir fired back at Owens to back up his teammate, who has fitted brilliantly despite only having joined the team this season. item.title: ‘Insufferable’ – Angel Reese receives fan hate for arguing with referee in Dream’s WNBA Finals loss
item.description: Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese had a rough time dealing with the referees and the physicality of the Golden State Valkyries in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals. Reese could not keep her Finals double-double streak alive with eight points and nine rebounds on 2-for-12 field goal shooting, and the Dream could not hold on to home-court advantage and lost Game 4 67-62. While Reese was receiving a lot of love as the frontrunner to win WNBA Finals MVP when the team held a 2-1 series lead, the sentiment around her seems to have shifted after her actions in the Game 4 loss. Angel Reese’s behaviour with the referee upset WNBA fans Reese confronted WNBA referees on the court at the end of the first half, clearly frustrated at the physicality with which the Valkyries played. Reese’s behaviour with the referee prompted many angry fan reactions, as they questioned why she was not penalised with a technical foul as many of her peers have been. “Angel Reese is an insufferable child,” complained one fan . “She behaves that way because she knows there won’t be any consequences,” said another fan . “She acts like a person who has been told her entire life that she is really special, she’s good. Not special,” said an angry fan . “That clapping by Reese in the ref’s face should have been an instant technical foul. No excuse,” is what another fan had to say . “I know Caitlin does this as well, but damn this —- is childish. All of them need techs called,” said another fan . The Dream received 31 free throw attempts compared to the Valkyries 13 in this game. The Dream would argue they deserved many more during the contest due to their inside-heavy offence and the physicality which was used to guard them. Reese only shot six free throws the entire game, so she potentially had some justified reasons to be frustrated with the officiating. Nonetheless, it was a bad look for her to lose her temper at the officials in such a visible moment of the game. item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. And we’ll set you up for the weekend and let you know our live coverage plans so you’ll be ahead of the game. Here’s what you can expect from us. Try our other sports emails: there’s daily football news and gossip in The Fiver , and weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown . Living in Australia?
